items.message: This change implements GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request force-pushes to the existing branch rather than opening a second pull request. The diff covers the full described behaviour — the update path in `implement_propose`, the `update_reviewable` helper, `GitHubScm.update_change` and `mark_draft`, `GitLabScm.update_change` and `mark_draft`, `GitLocal.fetch_branch`, the `_existing_change_for` and `_branch_state` helpers, and a test file that exercises al…[truncated]
GitLab `mark_draft` prefixes `change.title`, which may already carry `Draft:`.

`_existing_change_for` silently falls through to the new-PR path on `changes_for` errors, which the surrounding text says is the right behaviour — but `_branch_state` errors also return `None`, and the two `None` returns mean different things to the caller.

This change adds an update path for `/implement` when a change request already exists for the ticket: instead of opening a second pull request, it fetches the existing branch, checks for person-authored commits, and force-pushes with a lease keyed on the sha it read. The performance lens has little to find here — the new code is on a cold path (one `/implement` comment triggers it), and the operations involved (git fetch, git log, one or two GitHub API calls) are inherently network-bound and not…[truncated]

This change introduces the update-existing-change-request path for a second `/implement` run: it fetches the existing branch, checks for non-framework commits, and force-pushes with a lease on the sha it read. The security-relevant properties are the person-commit refusal guard, the force-with-lease binding, the unreadable-branch refusal, and the `assert_run_scoped` check on the branch before any write. I checked the trust boundary between what the check inspected and what the push acts on, the …[truncated]
git stderr, including remote URL with embedded credentials, forwarded to the public ticket comment.
Same git-stderr-to-ticket-comment exposure as the GitHub adapter.

This change introduces GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request force-pushes to the existing branch rather than opening a new one. The test file `test_update_existing_change.py` is substantial and carefully structured in two tiers — stub-level tests for routing logic and real-git tests for the adapter properties that stubs cannot falsify. I reviewed the full diff. The tests cover the named gate's ten promised test names, and the real-git tier addresses a speci…[truncated]
The 'cannot tell' message asserted does not match the text the code posts.
test_the_changeset_is_built_over_head_not_the_branch_tip calls GitHubScm directly but supplies no remote URL, gh binary, or token — the test may pass for the wrong reason.
No test covers _existing_change_for when changes_for raises — the fallback to the new-PR path.
test_a_red_second_attempt_puts_the_change_request_back_into_draft relies on no verdict being present, but 'no verdict' is not explicitly set — it depends on artifact layout.
